import sys, json, uuid, datetime, math, re

doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
d = doc["body"]
envelope = doc["envelope"]
h = envelope.get("header", {})
ctx = h.get("context", {})
hop = h.get("hop", {}) or {}
now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ")


def audience_of(raw):
    """`context.audience_set` as the participant SET it claims to be, or None.

    Normalised exactly the way affinity's gate normalises its own
    (deduplicated, blanks dropped, sorted): memory and affinity run the same
    subset rule over the same vocabulary, and an ordering difference between
    the two halves of one rule is a difference nobody can see. A JSON list
    arrives as text because context values are strings; a real list is accepted
    too, so a caller that promotes a structured value is not punished for it.
    """
    if isinstance(raw, list):
        items = raw
    else:
        try:
            items = json.loads(str(raw or ""))
        except Exception:
            return None
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return None
    return sorted({str(x) for x in items if str(x)})


# ------------------------------------------------------------ AFFECT MARK (GH #936)
# A recognizer elsewhere in the colony marks how a turn read -- valence,
# arousal, its own confidence and its name -- and this lane files the mark on
# the episode. The writer stays the hive's ONE writer of `episodes`; that is
# why the lane lands here and not in a cell of its own.
#
# The mark is written only when the asking round may READ the episode: a mark
# is a statement about a turn, and a round that could not see the turn must not
# learn that it exists by being allowed to annotate it. Unknown and invisible
# therefore answer the SAME `not_visible`, and the acknowledgement names no id
# the caller did not send itself and never carries the episode text.
#
# The last write wins: the column holds the current reading, not a history --
# a history of readings is the recognizer's business, not this memory's.
AFFECT_PHASES = ("affect", "affect-read", "affect-write")
AFFECT_KEYS = ("episode_id", "session_id", "turn_id", "valence", "arousal",
               "confidence", "source")
AFFECT_SOURCE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$")
# The longest correlation token a caller may hand through (`hop.affect_tag`).
AFFECT_TAG_MAX = 64
# An address longer than this is not an id this hive minted (uuid4 is 36).
AFFECT_ID_MAX = 200


def _id_ok(v):
    return isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() != "" and len(v) <= AFFECT_ID_MAX


def _in_range(v, lo, hi):
    # A bool is an int to Python and never a reading.
    if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return False
    return math.isfinite(v) and lo <= v <= hi


def parse_affect(a):
    """The `affect` object of an `in_affect` body -> (request, None), or
    (None, <key>) naming the first key that is wrong.

    Exactly one address: `episode_id`, OR `session_id` + `turn_id` (the turn
    key a recognizer reads off the sidecar). An unknown key is refused rather
    than ignored -- a field this lane would drop silently is a field a caller
    believes was filed. Numbers keep three decimals.
    """
    if not isinstance(a, dict):
        return None, "affect"
    for k in sorted(a):
        if k not in AFFECT_KEYS:
            return None, k
    req = {}
    by_id = "episode_id" in a
    by_turn = "session_id" in a or "turn_id" in a
    if by_id == by_turn:
        return None, "episode_id"
    if by_id:
        if not _id_ok(a["episode_id"]):
            return None, "episode_id"
        req["episode_id"] = a["episode_id"]
    else:
        for k in ("session_id", "turn_id"):
            if not _id_ok(a.get(k)):
                return None, k
            req[k] = a[k]
    for k, lo, hi in (("valence", -1, 1), ("arousal", 0, 1), ("confidence", 0, 1)):
        if not _in_range(a.get(k), lo, hi):
            return None, k
        req[k] = round(float(a[k]), 3)
    if not isinstance(a.get("source"), str) or not AFFECT_SOURCE.match(a["source"]):
        return None, "source"
    req["source"] = a["source"]
    return req, None


# The round and the stored participant set are read EXACTLY the way recall
# reads them (`recall/config.json`: `audience_of`, `read_audience_now` -- the
# bodies below are copies, and gh936 pins them byte-equal to recall's): a mark
# is a statement about a turn, so the round that may file one is the round that
# may recall it, never a wider one. Blank names are kept as recall keeps them --
# a round naming "" is a subset of no stored set, as in recall.
def stored_audience(value):
    """A participant set off the store: a JSON list in a text column. Anything
    that is not a JSON list reads as the EMPTY set, which is invisible to every
    non-empty round -- unreadable provenance is not a licence."""
    if isinstance(value, list):
        items = value
    else:
        try:
            items = json.loads(value or "[]")
        except Exception:
            return set()
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return set()
    return {str(i) for i in items}


def read_round(ctx):
    """The asking round, off `context.audience_now` (a JSON list the port edge
    promotes). None means "no audience given" and becomes a REJECT, never an
    empty set: the empty set is a subset of everything and would open the whole
    hive. An empty LIST is treated the same way, for exactly that reason."""
    raw = ctx.get("audience_now")
    if raw is None:
        return None
    if not isinstance(raw, list) and not str(raw).strip():
        return None
    got = stored_audience(raw)
    return got or None


def visible(round_set, ep_audience):
    """May this round READ the episode? recall's `visible` for an episode row:
    a row without participants is refused first, `*` is universal, otherwise
    the round must be a subset. No channel clause -- a mark is not a question
    asked in a room, so the open-history relaxation has nothing to relax
    (stricter than recall, never wider)."""
    aud = stored_audience(ep_audience)
    if not aud:
        return False
    if "*" in aud:
        return True
    if not round_set:
        return False
    return set(round_set) <= aud


def canonical_mark(req):
    return json.dumps({"valence": req["valence"], "arousal": req["arousal"],
                       "confidence": req["confidence"], "source": req["source"],
                       "at": req["at"]}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))


def affect_ack(episode_id, code, tag, key=""):
    """The one answer of the lane. Every outcome has the same keys, so the
    shape of a refusal says nothing a code does not."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
        [{"header": {"route": "affect_ack", "episode_id": episode_id,
                     "error_code": code, "error_key": key, "affect_tag": tag},
          "messages": [], "affect_ack": {"episode_id": episode_id}}]))
    sys.exit(0)


def affect_store(args, phase, episode_id, req):
    # `affect_req` rides the store round trip in context (the edge promotes it):
    # the store answers rows, not the request that asked for them.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
        [{"header": {"route": "astore", "phase": phase, "episode_id": episode_id,
                     "affect_req": json.dumps(req, sort_keys=True)},
          "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "w-" + phase,
                        "text": json.dumps(args)}]}]))
    sys.exit(0)


def handle_affect(phase):
    op = hop.get("operation")
    err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
    round_set = read_round(ctx)
    if err and op:
        # GH #343: a refusal is not a result -- the store did not read or write.
        # PP-S3-11: and it carries the caller's `affect_tag` like every
        # `affect_ack` does, out of the request that rode the store round trip
        # -- without it the refusal reached the caller with nothing that says
        # WHICH of its marks was refused, and an app with two marks in flight
        # could not tell its own failure from another's.
        try:
            pending = json.loads(str(ctx.get("affect_req") or ""))
        except Exception:
            pending = None
        tag = str((pending.get("tag") if isinstance(pending, dict) else None)
                  or hop.get("affect_tag") or "")[:AFFECT_TAG_MAX]
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
            [{"header": {"route": "reject", "episode_id": "",
                         "reject_reason": "store_refused", "store_error": err,
                         "store_operation": str(op), "affect_tag": tag},
              "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "w-reject",
                            "text": "affect mark not written: the store refused the %s "
                                    "with %s" % (op, err)}]}]))
        sys.exit(0)
    if phase == "affect":
        if op is not None:
            sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
            sys.exit(0)
        raw = d.get("affect")
        caller = raw.get("episode_id") if isinstance(raw, dict) else ""
        caller = caller if _id_ok(caller) else ""
        tag = str(hop.get("affect_tag") or "")
        # The round first (contract order): who asks decides what may be
        # touched, and a request without one is a wiring bug, not a bad value.
        if not round_set:
            affect_ack(caller, "missing_audience", tag[:AFFECT_TAG_MAX])
        req, key = parse_affect(raw)
        if key:
            affect_ack(caller, "invalid_input", tag[:AFFECT_TAG_MAX], key)
        if len(tag) > AFFECT_TAG_MAX:
            affect_ack(caller, "invalid_input", tag[:AFFECT_TAG_MAX], "affect_tag")
        req["tag"] = tag
        req["at"] = now
        if "episode_id" in req:
            where, order = {"id": req["episode_id"]}, []
        else:
            # The INCOMING turn of that turn id: the agent's own answer shares
            # the turn key and is never what a reading of the member is about.
            where = {"session_id": req["session_id"], "turn_id": req["turn_id"],
                     "sender": {"neq": "assistant"}}
            order = [{"col": "recorded_at", "dir": "asc"}, {"col": "id", "dir": "asc"}]
        args = {"operation": "select", "table": "episodes",
                "columns": ["id", "audience_set"], "where": where, "limit": 1}
        if order:
            args["order_by"] = order
        affect_store(args, "affect-read", req.get("episode_id", ""), req)
    try:
        req = json.loads(str(ctx.get("affect_req") or ""))
    except Exception:
        req = None
    if not isinstance(req, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("writer: an affect reply arrived without its request, dropped\n")
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
        sys.exit(0)
    caller = str(req.get("episode_id", "") or "")
    tag = str(req.get("tag", "") or "")
    if phase == "affect-read" and op == "select":
        try:
            rows = json.loads((d.get("messages") or [{}])[0].get("text") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            rows = []
        row = rows[0] if isinstance(rows, list) and rows and isinstance(rows[0], dict) else None
        # Unknown and invisible are ONE answer, and its id is the caller's own.
        if row is None or not visible(round_set, row.get("audience_set")):
            affect_ack(caller, "not_visible", tag)
        found = str(row.get("id") or "")
        req["resolved"] = found
        affect_store({"operation": "update", "table": "episodes",
                      "set": {"affect": canonical_mark(req)}, "where": {"id": found}},
                     "affect-write", found, req)
    if phase == "affect-write" and op == "update":
        found = str(req.get("resolved", "") or "")
        if int(hop.get("rows_affected", 0) or 0) < 1 or not found:
            # The row was there a hop ago and is gone now: still nothing to say
            # about it beyond what the caller already knew.
            affect_ack(caller, "not_visible", tag)
        affect_ack(found, "", tag)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


AFFECT_PHASE = str(ctx.get("mem_phase", "") or "")
if AFFECT_PHASE in AFFECT_PHASES:
    handle_affect(AFFECT_PHASE)
# ----------------------------------------------------------- /AFFECT MARK


# ------------------------------------------------ ALIASES FROM OUTSIDE (GH #948)
# Another part of the colony -- a hive that keeps rows about the things a
# member talks about -- names the spellings a thing goes by and the id it
# carries there: `{aliases: [{alias, canonical}], force?}`. The store already
# derives `facts.canonical_subject` from the alias table on every write and
# re-derives the whole column on `canonicalize`; this lane only writes rows of
# that table, so a fact said about "Firewall X" -- before the binding or after
# it -- answers to `ob-...` without a single fact being rewritten by hand.
#
# `set_alias` is an upsert without a check (store/ops.rs `op_set_alias`): a
# spelling the night already bound elsewhere would be moved silently. So the
# writer READS the alias table first, keyed in the STORE's normal form, and
# refuses a spelling that points at another id with `alias_taken` -- unless the
# caller says `force`. The writer stays the hive's one writer of caller-driven
# rows, which is why the lane lands here and not in a cell of its own.
#
# The read alone holds only while requests come one at a time: two requests for
# one spelling can both read the empty table before either writes (GH #948
# review I-1). So without `force` the write is a plain `insert` on the table's
# PRIMARY KEY (store/ddl.rs, `alias TEXT PRIMARY KEY`), never the upsert, and a
# `select` of the keys closes the same bundle. The store cell runs one message
# after the other (meclaw-colony cell_task.rs), so nothing lands between the
# insert and that select: an insert the key refused reads back as the id that
# won -- `alias_taken` -- or as the same id, which is bound all the same. The
# insert key is this script's copy of the normal form; gh948 pins it to the
# store's, and a drift between the two would leave a binding without effect
# (the store would look under another key), never move someone else's.
#
# The alias table carries no audience (store/config.json `canonical`): an alias
# says that a spelling MEANS an id, never what anybody said about it. The answer
# never names the previous target of a taken spelling: a target may be a
# subject the nightly identity round derived from conversations -- content of
# rounds the caller was never part of -- and no shape of the string tells that
# apart from an id; the caller knows its own ids from its own rows.
ALIAS_PHASES = ("alias", "alias-read", "alias-write")
ALIAS_KEYS = ("alias", "canonical")
ALIAS_MAX = 32
ALIAS_CHARS = 200
CANONICAL_CHARS = 64
# An id with a namespace: `<prefix>-<rest>`, lowercase ASCII only, so its store
# normal form is the id itself and a binding can never be split by spelling.
CANONICAL_ID = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9_-]+")
ALIAS_TAG_MAX = 64

# Byte twin of recall's `normalize_text` and of the store's own normal form
# (crates/meclaw-cells/src/store/query/normalize.rs) -- the key the alias table
# is written under. A script cannot import, so gh948 pins this copy against the
# store's function over one table and against recall's copy byte for byte: a
# check that keyed a spelling differently from the store would wave through
# exactly the rebinding it exists to refuse.
COMPOSE_ROWS = (
    ("\u0300", "aeiou", "\u00e0\u00e8\u00ec\u00f2\u00f9"),
    ("\u0301", "aeiouy", "\u00e1\u00e9\u00ed\u00f3\u00fa\u00fd"),
    ("\u0302", "aeiou", "\u00e2\u00ea\u00ee\u00f4\u00fb"),
    ("\u0303", "ano", "\u00e3\u00f1\u00f5"),
    ("\u0308", "aeiouy", "\u00e4\u00eb\u00ef\u00f6\u00fc\u00ff"),
    ("\u030a", "a", "\u00e5"),
    ("\u0327", "c", "\u00e7"),
)
COMPOSITIONS = {(base, mark): composed
                for mark, bases, composed_forms in COMPOSE_ROWS
                for base, composed in zip(bases, composed_forms)}
# Rust's `char::is_whitespace` (the Unicode White_Space property), spelled out:
# Python's `str.split()` also splits on U+001C..U+001F, which the store keeps.
WHITE_SPACE = frozenset("\t\n\x0b\x0c\r \x85\xa0\u1680\u2000\u2001\u2002\u2003"
                        "\u2004\u2005\u2006\u2007\u2008\u2009\u200a\u2028\u2029"
                        "\u202f\u205f\u3000")


def normalize_text(value):
    """The normal form of one string -- the twin of `meclaw_norm` (0.2.0 P4).

    Same three effects in the same order as the store: case fold, Latin-1
    composition (NFD -> NFC), whitespace collapse over the store's own
    whitespace. An unrecognised mark leaves the two spellings DIFFERENT, which
    is the same conservatism the Rust side ships.
    """
    out = []
    for ch in str(value or "").lower():
        composed = COMPOSITIONS.get((out[-1], ch)) if out else None
        if composed is None:
            out.append(ch)
        else:
            out[-1] = composed
    words, word = [], []
    for ch in out:
        if ch in WHITE_SPACE:
            if word:
                words.append("".join(word))
                word = []
        else:
            word.append(ch)
    if word:
        words.append("".join(word))
    return " ".join(words)


def parse_aliases(body):
    """The body of an `in_alias` request -> (entries, force, None), or
    (None, None, <key>) naming the first thing that is wrong, e.g.
    `aliases[2].canonical`.

    Whole or refused, like `parse_affect`: a request with one bad entry writes
    nothing, so a caller never has to guess which half of its list landed. An
    unknown key in an entry is refused rather than ignored.
    """
    if not isinstance(body, dict):
        return None, None, "aliases"
    aliases = body.get("aliases")
    if not isinstance(aliases, list) or not 1 <= len(aliases) <= ALIAS_MAX:
        return None, None, "aliases"
    force = body.get("force", False)
    if not isinstance(force, bool):
        return None, None, "force"
    entries = []
    for i, item in enumerate(aliases):
        at = "aliases[%d]" % i
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            return None, None, at
        for k in sorted(item):
            if k not in ALIAS_KEYS:
                return None, None, "%s.%s" % (at, k)
        alias = item.get("alias")
        if not isinstance(alias, str) or not 1 <= len(alias) <= ALIAS_CHARS:
            return None, None, at + ".alias"
        key = normalize_text(alias)
        if not key:
            return None, None, at + ".alias"
        canonical = item.get("canonical")
        if (not isinstance(canonical, str) or len(canonical) > CANONICAL_CHARS
                or not CANONICAL_ID.fullmatch(canonical)):
            return None, None, at + ".canonical"
        entries.append({"alias": alias, "key": key, "canonical": canonical})
    return entries, force, None


def judge_aliases(entries, force, held):
    """(binds, refused) for the entries of one request, given `held` -- the
    alias table's rows for their keys, `{key: canonical}` in store normal form.

    In request order, as if each entry were written before the next is judged:
    two entries of one request that claim one spelling for two ids are the same
    conflict as a spelling the table already holds (the first wins; `force`
    lets the last win, which is also what the store's upserts do in order). The
    same id again is no conflict -- binding is idempotent.
    """
    held = dict(held)
    binds, refused = [], []
    for e in entries:
        previous = held.get(e["key"])
        if previous is not None and previous != e["canonical"] and not force:
            refused.append({"alias": e["alias"], "error_code": "alias_taken"})
            continue
        binds.append(e)
        held[e["key"]] = e["canonical"]
    return binds, refused


def alias_ack(done, refused, code, tag, key=""):
    """The one answer of the lane. Every outcome carries the same keys --
    `done` (spellings bound by this request), `refused` (`{alias, error_code}`
    each, never the previous target) -- and the hop says
    what happened: '' bound, 'invalid_input' (nothing written, `error_key`
    names the place), 'store_refused' (the store said no; `error_key` names
    the op)."""
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
        [{"header": {"route": "alias_ack", "episode_id": "", "error_code": code,
                     "error_key": key, "alias_tag": tag},
          "messages": [], "done": done, "refused": refused}]))
    sys.exit(0)


def alias_store(calls, phase, req):
    # `alias_req` rides the store round trip in context (the edge promotes it),
    # exactly like `affect_req`: the store answers rows, not the request.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
        [{"header": {"route": "alstore", "phase": phase, "episode_id": "",
                     "alias_req": json.dumps(req, sort_keys=True)},
          "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": cid,
                        "text": json.dumps(args)} for cid, args in calls]}]))
    sys.exit(0)


def handle_alias(phase):
    op = hop.get("operation")
    err = str(hop.get("error_code", "") or "")
    if phase == "alias":
        if op is not None:
            sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
            sys.exit(0)
        tag = str(hop.get("alias_tag") or "")
        if len(tag) > ALIAS_TAG_MAX:
            alias_ack(0, [], "invalid_input", tag[:ALIAS_TAG_MAX], "alias_tag")
        entries, force, bad = parse_aliases(d)
        if bad:
            alias_ack(0, [], "invalid_input", tag, bad)
        keys = sorted({e["key"] for e in entries})
        alias_store([("al-read", {"operation": "select", "table": "subject_aliases",
                                  "columns": ["alias", "canonical"],
                                  "where": {"alias": {"in": keys}}})],
                    "alias-read", {"entries": entries, "force": force, "tag": tag})
    try:
        req = json.loads(str(ctx.get("alias_req") or ""))
    except Exception:
        req = None
    if not isinstance(req, dict):
        sys.stderr.write("writer: an alias reply arrived without its request, dropped\n")
        sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
        sys.exit(0)
    tag = str(req.get("tag", "") or "")
    if phase == "alias-read" and op is not None:
        if err:
            # GH #343: a refusal is not a result -- nothing was read, so nothing
            # may be judged, and nothing is written.
            alias_ack(0, [], "store_refused", tag, str(op))
        try:
            rows = json.loads((d.get("messages") or [{}])[0].get("text") or "[]")
        except Exception:
            rows = []
        held = {}
        for r in rows if isinstance(rows, list) else []:
            if isinstance(r, dict) and isinstance(r.get("alias"), str):
                held[r["alias"]] = str(r.get("canonical") or "")
        force = bool(req.get("force"))
        binds, refused = judge_aliases(req.get("entries") or [], force, held)
        if not binds:
            alias_ack(0, refused, "", tag)
        # The write of each bound spelling: `force` is the upsert; otherwise an
        # unbound key is an `insert` (the key refuses a second one, see the head
        # of this block) and a key that already means this id writes nothing.
        # Then ONE canonicalize over the subject column -- the store re-derives
        # every fact from the table as it now stands, so the facts said before
        # this request and those said after it read the same id -- and last the
        # select that settles every spelling. The bundle runs in call order over
        # one connection, with no foreign message in between.
        calls, plan, planned = [], [], set()
        for i, e in enumerate(binds):
            if force:
                write = "set_alias"
                calls.append(("al-%d" % i, {"operation": "set_alias", "table": "facts",
                                            "column": "subject", "alias": e["alias"],
                                            "canonical": e["canonical"], "recorded_at": now}))
            elif e["key"] in held or e["key"] in planned:
                write = ""
            else:
                write = "insert"
                planned.add(e["key"])
                calls.append(("al-%d" % i, {"operation": "insert", "table": "subject_aliases",
                                            "row": {"alias": e["key"], "canonical": e["canonical"],
                                                    "recorded_at": now}}))
            plan.append({"alias": e["alias"], "key": e["key"],
                         "canonical": e["canonical"], "write": write})
        calls.append(("al-canon", {"operation": "canonicalize", "table": "facts",
                                   "column": "subject"}))
        calls.append(("al-check", {"operation": "select", "table": "subject_aliases",
                                   "columns": ["alias", "canonical"],
                                   "where": {"alias": {"in": sorted({e["key"] for e in binds})}}}))
        alias_store(calls, "alias-write", {"binds": plan, "refused": refused, "tag": tag})
    if phase == "alias-write" and op is not None:
        binds = [b for b in req.get("binds") or [] if isinstance(b, dict)]
        refused = list(req.get("refused") or [])
        if err:
            # A wholesale refusal of the bundle: no leg ran.
            refused.extend({"alias": str(b.get("alias", "")), "error_code": "store_refused"}
                           for b in binds)
            alias_ack(0, refused, "store_refused", tag, str(op))
        results, texts = {}, {}
        for r in d.get("results") or []:
            if isinstance(r, dict):
                results[str(r.get("tool_call_id") or "")] = r
        for m in d.get("messages") or []:
            if isinstance(m, dict):
                texts[str(m.get("id") or "")] = m.get("text")
        # What the table says now, after this bundle's own writes; None when
        # the closing select was refused (then no insert that lost is judged).
        table = None
        check = results.get("al-check")
        if check is not None and not check.get("error_code"):
            try:
                rows = json.loads(texts.get("al-check") or "[]")
            except Exception:
                rows = None
            if isinstance(rows, list):
                table = {}
                for r in rows:
                    if isinstance(r, dict) and isinstance(r.get("alias"), str):
                        table[r["alias"]] = str(r.get("canonical") or "")
        done, landed_keys = 0, set()
        for i, b in enumerate(binds):
            alias, write = str(b.get("alias", "")), str(b.get("write", ""))
            key = str(b.get("key", ""))
            leg = results.get("al-%d" % i) if write else None
            landed = leg is not None and not leg.get("error_code")
            if write == "set_alias" or landed:
                # The upsert is its own verdict; an insert that landed is bound,
                # and so is a later entry of this request for that key.
                if landed:
                    done += 1
                    landed_keys.add(key)
                else:
                    refused.append({"alias": alias, "error_code": "store_refused"})
                continue
            if not write and key in landed_keys:
                done += 1
                continue
            now_held = None if table is None else table.get(key)
            if now_held is not None and now_held == b.get("canonical"):
                done += 1
            elif now_held is not None:
                # Another request bound the spelling between this read and this
                # write, and its insert came first.
                refused.append({"alias": alias, "error_code": "alias_taken"})
            else:
                refused.append({"alias": alias, "error_code": "store_refused"})
        canon = results.get("al-canon")
        if canon is None or canon.get("error_code"):
            # The spellings stand, the facts were not re-derived: the next
            # canonicalize (this lane's or the night's) completes it.
            alias_ack(done, refused, "store_refused", tag, "canonicalize")
        alias_ack(done, refused, "", tag)
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


if AFFECT_PHASE in ALIAS_PHASES:
    handle_alias(AFFECT_PHASE)
# ------------------------------------------------ /ALIASES FROM OUTSIDE

turn = None
for m in d.get("messages", []):
    # GH #849 (owner ruling R-SN-4): a `peer` turn -- another participant of a
    # peer or group channel -- is remembered in full like the other two. Before
    # it, it fell through this filter without a trace.
    if m.get("type") == "text" and m.get("origin") in ("user", "assistant", "peer"):
        turn = m
        break
if turn is None:
    # Echo guard: store replies and non-conversational input end here.
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps([]))
    sys.exit(0)


def refuse(reason, text):
    """The write path's fail-closed exit (#244, ADR-0002 E2).

    A turn whose provenance is incomplete is neither written with a guess nor
    dropped in silence: NOTHING reaches the store, the hive's `reject` lane
    carries `hop.reject_reason`, and the caller learns the memory was not
    written. An untagged row cannot be tagged later honestly -- the audience of
    an episode is the participant set of the conversation it happened in, and
    nobody downstream can reconstruct that -- so the only honest answers are
    "written with its audience" and "refused".

    The header carries the same key set as the two success lanes plus the
    reason, so a parent edge can promote it on either lane without a missing
    key making its CEL modifier fail (a failed modifier skips the whole edge).
    """
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(
        [{"header": {"route": "reject", "episode_id": "", "reject_reason": reason},
          "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result", "id": "w-reject",
                        "text": text}]}]))
    sys.exit(0)


# Kantenwahrheit, not a body claim: both keys are promoted to context by the
# edge that carries the turn in, which is why a turn cannot assert its own
# audience (the reason affinity/brief reads its asker from context as well).
audience = audience_of(ctx.get("audience_set"))
if not audience:
    refuse("missing_audience",
           "episode refused: context.audience_set is missing, empty, or not a "
           "non-empty JSON list of participants. Who was present is the gate on "
           "every later read of this turn, it cannot be inferred from the turn "
           "itself, and an untagged row stands permanently outside the rule")
channel = str(ctx.get("channel", "") or "")
if not channel:
    refuse("missing_channel",
           "episode refused: context.channel is missing. The room is stored "
           "explicitly and never parsed out of the session_id prefix -- that "
           "prefix is a convention of the session-keeper, not a promise to this "
           "hive -- and without it the channel-local clause of the read rule "
           "has no left-hand side")

content = turn.get("text", "")
episode_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
session_id = str(ctx.get("session_id", "default"))
turn_id = str(ctx.get("turn_id", episode_id))
origin = turn.get("origin", "user")
# WHO spoke, in affinity vocabulary (`member:<name>` / `agent:<name>`). `sender`
# keeps the ROLE and `speaker` carries the IDENTITY; the two answer different
# questions and neither replaces the other. Translating a connector's own user
# id into that vocabulary happens on the edge of the talky (ADR-0002 E8) -- this
# hive never looks anything up. Absent, it stays empty: a role written into an
# identity column is exactly the defect this column exists to end.
#
# OPTIONAL, unlike the audience (contract ruling R1). The audience is the
# security-bearing field; the speaker is provenance detail. Refusing a turn
# because a participant id has not been mapped to a person yet would make the
# ingress brittle exactly where the mapping is hardest -- at the newcomer nobody
# has named. Better the episode with the right audience and an empty speaker
# than no episode at all.
#
# GH #849: a PEER turn names its speaker on the turn itself -- `speaker_ref`, the
# participant reference affinity mints, which the collector hands through with
# every such turn. That reference is who said it and becomes the `source` of
# every fact extracted from it. Absent, the column stays empty: a peer's words
# are never filed under the agent's own id, which would make them the agent's.
if origin == "peer":
    speaker = str(turn.get("speaker_ref") or "")
else:
    speaker = str((ctx.get("speaker") if origin == "user" else ctx.get("agent_id")) or "")
audience_set = json.dumps(audience)

# Event time may come from the caller (context.happened_at, promoted from hop by
# the port edge); system time is always ours. That split IS the bi-temporal model.
happened_at = str(ctx.get("happened_at") or "") or now
episode = {"operation": "insert", "table": "episodes",
           "row": {"id": episode_id, "session_id": session_id, "turn_id": turn_id,
                   "sender": origin, "speaker": speaker, "channel": channel,
                   "audience_set": audience_set, "content": content,
                   "happened_at": happened_at, "recorded_at": now}}
# The audience travels WITH the queue item, so the extraction lane inherits the
# participant set of the turn it is extracting instead of re-deriving it.
queue_item = {"episode_id": episode_id, "session_id": session_id,
              "channel": channel, "audience_set": audience_set,
              "sender": origin, "speaker": speaker, "content": content,
              "token_est": max(1, len(content) // 4)}
# GH #519: the episode gets a vector of its own. Two halves, and the split is
# the one `./extract-glue` already uses for a fact -- the QUEUED row is written
# first and unconditionally, in the same store bundle as the episode, and the
# embed call beside it is the optional part. A night that finds a null blob
# fills it; a run where the embedder is down loses a call, never a row.
#
# An episode used to be the only durable object in this hive without an
# embedding, which made the semantic leg of the tier-1 fan a fact-only leg --
# and an episode is raw conversational text, exactly the material a lexical
# index is worst at and a vector is best at.
#
# No lookup is needed for the text: this cell wrote the content, so the embed
# call carries it rather than sending the lane back to the store for it.
embedding_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
embedding = {"operation": "insert", "table": "embeddings",
             "row": {"id": embedding_id, "owner_table": "episodes",
                     "owner_id": episode_id, "model_id": "", "dim": 0,
                     "binarization_version": "", "blob": None,
                     "status": "queued", "created_at": now}}
out = [{"header": {"route": "wstore", "episode_id": episode_id},
        "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "w-ep",
                      "text": json.dumps(episode)},
                     {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "w-emb",
                      "text": json.dumps(embedding)}]},
       {"header": {"route": "enqueue", "episode_id": episode_id},
        "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "text",
                      "text": json.dumps(queue_item)}]}]
# An empty turn carries no signal to embed. The row is still minted above --
# the queue is the durable half and a night can decide otherwise -- but nothing
# is sent to a paid embedder over an empty string.
if content.strip():
    out.append({"header": {"route": "embed", "episode_id": episode_id},
                "messages": [{"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "w-embed",
                              "text": json.dumps({"items": [
                                  {"embedding_id": embedding_id, "text": content}]})}]})
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(out))

affect_ack.description: GH #936: `{episode_id}` on `affect_ack` -- the id the caller sent, or the resolved one once the mark is written. Never the episode text.

done.description: GH #948, on `alias_ack`: how many spellings of the request are bound now (an id bound again counts).

refused.description: GH #948, on `alias_ack`: `{alias, error_code}` per spelling not bound -- `alias_taken` (it means another id -- which one is never named: the alias table has no round, and a target may be a subject the night derived from conversations) or `store_refused`.

phase.description: GH #936: the step of an `in_affect` round trip on `astore` (`affect-read`, `affect-write`); GH #948: of an `in_alias` round trip on `alstore` (`alias-read`, `alias-write`). The edge to the store promotes it to `context.mem_phase`.

affect_req.description: GH #936: the mark request as JSON text on `astore`. The store answers rows, not the request that asked for them, so the edge carries it through the round trip in context. It holds the reading and the address, never episode text.

error_code.description: GH #936, on `affect_ack`: '' (written), 'not_visible' (unknown OR not readable by the asking round -- one answer for both, no existence oracle), 'missing_audience' (no round), 'invalid_input' (a key out of form or range, named in `error_key`). GH #948, on `alias_ack`: '' (judged and written), 'invalid_input' (nothing written, `error_key` names the place), 'store_refused' (`error_key` names the op).

error_key.description: GH #936, on `affect_ack`: the request key `invalid_input` refers to; '' otherwise. GH #948, on `alias_ack`: the place, e.g. `aliases[2].canonical`, or the store op a refusal refers to. Every acknowledgement carries the same keys.

affect_tag.description: GH #936, on `affect_ack` -- and, since PP-S3-11, on the `reject` of a store refusal on the affect lane: the caller's `hop.affect_tag` (at most 64 characters) echoed untouched, so one recognizer can match answers and refusals to requests.

store_error.description: GH #343/#936: the store's own `error_code` beside `reject_reason: store_refused` when an `in_affect` read or write was refused.

store_operation.description: GH #343/#936: the op the store refused.

alias_req.description: GH #948: the alias request as JSON text on `alstore` -- the entries and, after the read, what is bound and what was refused. The edge carries it through the store round trip in context, like `affect_req`.

alias_tag.description: GH #948, on `alias_ack`: the caller's `hop.alias_tag` (at most 64 characters) echoed, so a caller with two requests in flight can tell the answers apart.

affect.description: GH #936: the mark of an `in_affect` request -- `episode_id` OR `session_id`+`turn_id`, `valence` -1..1, `arousal` 0..1, `confidence` 0..1, `source` [a-z0-9-]{1,64}. An unknown key is refused.

aliases.description: GH #948: the entries of an `in_alias` request, 1..32 `{alias, canonical}` -- `alias` 1..200 characters, `canonical` an id `<prefix>-<rest>` of at most 64 characters from [a-z0-9_-]. An unknown key is refused.

force.description: GH #948: bind a spelling even when it already means another id.

audience_now.description: GH #936: the asking round of an `in_affect` request (a JSON list). A mark is written only on an episode this round may read.

mem_phase.description: GH #936: `affect`, `affect-read`, `affect-write` -- the steps of the mark round trip; GH #948: `alias`, `alias-read`, `alias-write` -- the steps of the alias round trip; every other value leaves the turn path as it was.

affect_req.description: GH #936: the request, carried through the store round trip by the edge.

alias_req.description: GH #948: the alias request, carried through the store round trip by the edge.

description.purpose: The shipped memory-hive writer, pinned for the memory-drain colony test (GH #125): it normalises one conversational turn into an append-only episodes row.
description.use_when: Test fixture only. cell, params and contract are the shipped values byte for byte -- the script under test is the real one. The private test x2_hive_fixture_drift.rs holds them against the living template.
description.not_in_scope: Not a template. This description is the fixture's own; the shipped one carries hive-internal wording that the public drain contract does not document.
